title: Mollusc shell pattern rules are effectively random, not optimized

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Mollusc shell pattern rules are effectively random, not optimized

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The rules generating mollusc shell patterns are effectively chosen at random from the simplest possibilities rather than optimized against predators or for mates, as shown by many species whose patterns are hidden by opaque skin throughout life.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: these patterns are instead generated by rules that are in effect chosen at random from among a collection of the simplest possibilities.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Biological Pigmentation Patterns” (from p. 422), p. 425. Scope: evolution of mollusc shell pigmentation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-27: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.36

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing occurrence, image, and phylogenetic resources can test whether patterns are visible and phylogenetically structured in restricted groups. They contain little direct evidence about rule choice, predation, mating, or fitness. Thus some adaptive alternatives can be tested, but the random-rule explanation remains weakly identified.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across mollusc phylogenies, compare shell-pattern visibility, predator and mate exposure, fitness associations, and inferred developmental-rule transitions against a neutral random-choice model over explicitly defined simple rules. Strong repeated fitness effects and nonneutral transitions would refute random choice.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fitness and exposure data are sparse across species.

A random distribution over generating rules is undefined.

Hidden patterns can have pleiotropic, developmental, or nonvisual functions.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Permanently covered patterns are a natural comparison that existing photographs and taxonomic descriptions can support for many species. The comparison is informative against selection for being seen, and it is silent about other functions. Compiling opacity and complexity across molluscs is a real curation task, so the test is partial rather than immediate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the distribution of pattern complexity between species whose shells stay covered by an opaque layer and species whose patterns are visible, against the distribution of the simplest cellular-automaton rules. Similar complexity in permanently hidden patterns would weaken optimization for visibility; a restriction of complex patterns to visible shells would count against the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Opacity and pattern are recorded in scattered descriptions, not in one coded dataset.

A hidden pattern could still be a side effect of selection on a linked visible or structural trait.
